question: What is Sculpt-Paint Wheel?
answer: A Blender add-on that shows your brushes and tools on a radial wheel right under your cursor. Hold Space in a sculpt or paint mode, pick a brush or button, and keep working, without reaching for toolbars or the asset shelf.

question: Which modes does it support?
answer: Sculpt, Vertex Paint, Weight Paint, Texture Paint, Sculpt Curves (hair), and the four Grease Pencil modes: Draw, Sculpt, Weight Paint and Vertex Paint. Each mode has its own wheel.

question: Which Blender versions are supported?
answer: Blender 5.1 and newer.

question: Does it work with Blender 4.x?
answer: Not this version. It's built as a Blender 5.x extension and relies on the brush assets and Grease Pencil system that Blender 5 uses.

question: How do I install it?
answer:
1. Download spwheel-<version>.zip from your Superhive library. Don't unzip it.
  2. In Blender, go to Edit › Preferences › Get Extensions, open the v menu at the top right and choose Install from Disk.... You can also drag and drop the zip into Blender.
  3. Make sure Sculpt-Paint Wheel is enabled under Edit › Preferences › Add-ons.

question: How do I update?
answer: Install the newer zip the same way. Your brush sets, custom buttons, scripts, themes and preferences are kept.

question: Does it work on Windows, macOS and Linux?
answer: It's built only on Blender's own Python and drawing APIs, with no platform-specific code, so it's available on every platform Blender supports. If something looks wrong on your system, message me here on Superhive.

question: Does it need internet access?
answer: No. The add-on only reads and writes its own files on your computer: its settings, your custom button scripts and your themes.

question: How do I open the wheel?
answer: Hover the 3D Viewport in a supported mode and hold Space. Pick a brush or button with a left click, then release Space. Esc or a right click closes the wheel without picking anything.

question: Space used to play the animation. What happened?
answer: In sculpt and paint modes, the add-on binds Space to the wheel, which takes priority over Blender's play shortcut there. Playback still works with Space in other modes and from the Timeline. If you'd rather use a different key, see the next question.

question: Can I change the hotkey?
answer: Yes. Open the add-on preferences and go to the Keymap tab, or go to Edit › Preferences › Keymap, search for Sculpt-Paint Wheel Modal, and change the key for the modes you want.

question: Can I pick a brush just by releasing the key?
answer: Yes. Turn on Select on Release in the add-on preferences: press Space, move toward a brush, release, done. Keep Open does the opposite: the wheel stays open after you release the key until you press it again.

question: Some of my brushes don't fit on the wheel.
answer:
When a set has more brushes than fit on the ring, the wheel gets pages. Scroll the mouse wheel, or click the arrows of the ‹ 1 / 2 › pill under the wheel, to switch between them.

You can also turn on Allow Double Ring in the add-on preferences (Settings tab, Brush Ring). Sets that don't fit on one ring then use two rings, and the wheel grows to fit them. Slots per Page there shows how many brushes fit.

question: How do I switch brush sets from the wheel?
answer: Drag the set name at the top of the wheel left or right, or use Shift + mouse wheel.

question: Can I change the brush size from the wheel?
answer: Yes. Press in the center of the wheel and drag up or down to change the brush radius, or left and right to change the strength. Hold Shift for finer steps or Ctrl for faster ones. Esc or a right click puts the values back.

question: Why doesn't Weight Paint show brushes?
answer: The Weight Paint wheels (mesh and Grease Pencil) show a weight dial instead of a brush list: pick any weight from 0.0 to 1.0 in one gesture. The round buttons under the dial switch weight paint tools, such as Blur or Smear.

question: How do I change which brushes and buttons appear?
answer: Open the sidebar with N in the 3D Viewport and go to the Wheel tab while you are in the mode you want to change. Brush Sets controls the outer ring and Custom Button Sets controls the center. See Customizing brushes and buttons.

question: What can a custom button do?
answer: It can run an operator, for example inverting the mask, or open a panel or menu as a popup, for example Stroke or Falloff settings. It can also toggle a setting such as Mirror X and show whether it's on, or run your own Python script. Each mode offers ready-made presets, and you can enter any panel, menu, operator or property by hand. A set holds up to 10 buttons.

question: Can I go back to the default setup?
answer: Yes. The default set is only created when a mode has no sets at all. Remove your sets for that mode in the Wheel tab, and the Default Set is recreated the next time Blender starts. In Sculpt Mode, Default Set (Masking) is only added once and doesn't come back if you remove it.

question: Where are my settings saved?
answer: In preferences.json, inside an spwheel folder in Blender's user folder for your Blender version, next to its config and scripts folders. It's written automatically when Blender closes, and whenever you press Save/Backup Addon Preferences in the add-on preferences. It's restored after you update or reinstall the extension. The same folder holds your custom button scripts (scripts) and your saved themes (themes).

question: Can I change the wheel's colors?
answer: Yes. In the add-on preferences, open the Theme tab. Pick one of the 10 built-in themes, such as Dark, Light or High Contrast, or edit the colors and use Save As to keep them as your own theme.

question: Nothing happens when I press Space.
answer:
• Make sure the mouse is over the 3D Viewport and you are in a supported mode: the wheel doesn't open in Object or Edit mode.
  • There must be an active object.
  • Check Edit › Preferences › Keymap for another add-on using Space in the same mode.
  • Make sure the extension is enabled under Edit › Preferences › Add-ons.

question: A button doesn't do anything.
answer: Some operators only work in the right context. For example, multires buttons need a Multires modifier, and keyframe buttons need an existing keyframe. When an operator can't run, Blender doesn't apply it and may print the reason in the system console.

question: The Falloff button opens a "Shape" panel.
answer: That's expected on Blender 5.3. Blender moved brush falloff into the new Shape panel for mesh sculpt and paint modes, and the add-on opens it automatically.

question: I found a bug.
answer: Message me here on Superhive. Include your Blender version, the mode you were in, the steps to reproduce it, and any error from Window › Toggle System Console (Windows) or the terminal (macOS/Linux).
